The Story to Tell Your Prospect

If you asked every manager in your organisation what eats the most time, status updates would almost always be in the top three. "Where is this up to?" "Did that get done?" "Can everyone join the call Thursday to go through progress?" It's a constant overhead — and for most businesses, it costs thousands of hours a year across the management team.

"A manager's job is to make decisions that move the business forward. But in most companies, they spend more time finding out what's happening than acting on it."

The Meeting Tax

Consider a five-person team with a weekly one-hour status meeting. That's 5 hours of collective time — every single week — just to update each other on what's already happened. Over a year, that's 260 hours. If the average salary is £35,000, that's roughly £4,300 a year spent in one weekly meeting, alone.

Now add the emails sent asking for updates. The messages chasing deadlines. The time spent preparing for meetings. The context-switching that comes with all of it. The real cost of traditional project management is easily three to four times what most managers estimate.

Analogy to use: "Running a business without a real-time project dashboard is like driving a car with a blindfold on and someone in the back seat shouting directions based on where you were five minutes ago. Automation gives you the windscreen back."

What Changes With Automation

When project management is automated, tasks are assigned the moment they become relevant — triggered by events like a deal being closed, a project being kicked off, or a deadline being set. Every team member knows exactly what they need to do, by when, and why. No email chains required.

Progress is tracked in real time. A manager can see the status of every project, every task, and every person in 30 seconds — without speaking to anyone. And instead of waiting for the weekly meeting to find out a deadline is at risk, the system sends a notification the moment it detects a problem.

The Financial Outcome

A manager on £35,000 a year costs roughly £16.80 an hour. If they're spending 1.5 hours every day on PM admin — chasing, updating, meeting — that's approximately £25 a day, over £6,500 a year, going into overhead. For a three-manager team, that's nearly £20,000 a year in management capacity lost to process friction.

"We don't just save meeting time. We give your managers the visibility to make better decisions faster — and that has a compounding effect on everything the business delivers."

What to Emphasise

  • Visibility: Real-time dashboards mean leaders always know what's happening — without having to ask.
  • Accountability: Automated task assignment with deadlines creates clear ownership from day one.
  • Meeting reduction: When status is always visible, most meetings become unnecessary.
  • Deadline protection: Automated reminders mean nothing slips through the cracks.
Walk Through This With Your Prospect

Common answers: emails, spreadsheets, weekly meetings. Each one is a signal that visibility is a problem.

Talking Points
On meetings
"If your team knows what's happening in real time, the status meeting becomes optional. Most businesses could eliminate half their meetings with the right dashboard."
On accountability
"When a task is assigned automatically with a deadline and an owner, nothing falls through the cracks. When it's assigned via email — things get missed."
On decisions
"Your managers should be making decisions, not collecting information to make decisions. Automation gives them the information instantly so they can act."
On scale
"As you take on more clients and projects, manual tracking breaks down. Automated systems scale with you — without adding management overhead."
Objection Handlers
"We already use Asana / Monday / Trello" +

Those tools are great — but they still require manual input. What we add is the automation layer on top: tasks that create themselves when triggers happen, notifications that send without anyone setting them, dashboards that update without anyone touching them. Your tool becomes active, not passive.

"Our projects are too complex to automate" +

Complex projects aren't automated — they're managed better. Automation handles the administrative overhead: task creation, deadline reminders, status notifications, progress tracking. The actual project decisions and problem-solving stay with your team. We just remove the noise around them.
